newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia clarifies share ownership confusion.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia clarifies share ownership confusion.

text.p: Indonesian Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad has reaffirmed that there is no regulation which limits share ownership on the country's two stock exchanges.

"In the capital market law there is no regulation that limits share ownership," Mar'ie said in a statement received on Friday. "The only restriction is the one which limits foreign ownership up to 49 percent of the listed shares on the exchanges."
The statement followed confusion in the markets after the Cooperatives and Small Business Minister Subiyakto Tjakrawerdaya met President Suharto on Wednesday.
Tjakrawerdaya quoted Suharto as saying individual shareholders in a private company going public should not hold more than 15 percent of the equity.

He declined to name any specific company, but it appeared from the context he was referring to the issue of Indonesia's largest car maker, Astra International, which had been the target of a bidding war in recent weeks.
Mar'ie said his statement reaffirmed that capital market activity was still governed by the 1995 capital market law.
